question: What is the most common cause of reversible/treatable visual impairment in elderly Indians?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. AMD is a major cause of irreversible vision loss in the elderly but is not the most common treatable cause in India.
Incorrect. Diabetic retinopathy is an important cause but is less prevalent than cataract in the elderly Indian population.
Correct. Cataract is the leading cause of visual impairment in elderly Indians and is surgically reversible — accounting for the majority of avoidable blindness in this population.
Incorrect. Glaucoma causes progressive irreversible optic nerve damage. While important, it is not the most common cause of treatable visual impairment in elderly India.

overallFeedback.feedback: Cataract is the most common and treatable cause of visual impairment in elderly Indians. AMD and glaucoma cause irreversible loss; cataract is surgically correctable.
Correct. Cataract is the most common cause of treatable visual impairment in Indian elderly. Surgical removal restores vision in most cases.
